comments: Child is correcting the assignment of an item in response to MOT's question 'für wen is(t) das?' (line 4172).
The token 'alle' in 'alle raus' is used as a quantifier meaning 'all/everything', not as a negation meaning 'all gone'.
Child rejects Mother's proposal to drive the stroller ('ich soll mit dem Kinderwagen fahr(e)n?'), explaining they have a rabbit.
Child opposes the placement of a figure during the activity of setting them up ('hinstellen').
Child rejects the mother's proposed manner of lying down ('noch mal so?'), vetoing the proposed action.
Child rejects the location of picking up the item/stool, proposing an alternative location ('nicht hier... hier').

Child corrects the identity of the person they want to show the car to, responding to the adult's correction in line 125899.
Child opposes Thorsten's claim to the toy ('ich krieg(e) den Flipper') by stating he already has it; toy dispute suggests Rejection.
Child refuses Opa's prompts to take the toy ('nimm doch') and come closer ('komm mal hier').
Child denies the mother's question 'is der für n Papi?' and asserts it is their own money ('mein deld').
Child denies the truth of the question 'kriegen wir das jetz(t), das Geld?'
Child rejects the directive to move over ('wir müssen rüber rücken').

Child denies the mother's claim that she has poop in her pants (line 250007).

Child reports that the toy phone is broken and does not work ('das is(t) kaputt', 'geht nich(t)'), which is a factual claim about the object's state.
Child questions the adult's claim that they are 'schon fertig' (finished), asking if there is not more available.
Child remarks that the lid is missing, repeating the claim from line 281769.
Child contradicts mother's claim in line 282477 that the animal is born.
Child opposes the dog having a ball in its mouth after Mother's observation in line 282611.

The token 'alle' is used as a quantifier meaning 'all of them' (confirmed by GIS: 'du willst alles haben?'), not as a negation meaning 'all gone'.

Child rejects the mother's directive to tidy up ('einräum(e)n'), confirmed by subsequent 'ich will noch weiter machen'.
Child reports that something 'doesn't work' (geht nicht) while tidying up; this is a factual claim about a failed action, which is coded as Denial.
Child reports that something does not work/fit while tidying up; factual claim about the object.
